content.short: Pomelo blends fee-free remittances with credit cards, letting US senders fund cards for family abroad.
content.description: Pomelo is a US fintech that reinvents remittances by combining money transfers with credit cards, letting families send money abroad while building credit at home. A sender in the United States opens a Pomelo account with a credit line and issues cards to family members overseas, initially focused on the Philippines, so recipients can spend directly with no transfer fees and rewards points along the way. Banking services come from a partner bank, and Pomelo settles the international leg through payment networks. By turning remittances into instant, card-based spending backed by credit rather than slow, fee-heavy wires, it targets immigrant families who regularly support relatives abroad and want a cheaper, more rewarding way to do it.
